title: Zscaler's AWS AI Guard examples (Lambda decorator, boto3 Bedrock hook, AgentCore guard, Strands hooks): seats, the shared scan client, verdict and failure handling

prose.text: The AWS folder of Zscaler's integration examples holds four single-file Python integrations that call the DAS detection API directly, without the Zscaler SDK. This subject covers what they share; each has its own subject. {{seats}} {{stdlib-only}}

prose.label: What does not reach AI Guard.
prose.text: {{identity-not-sent}} {{session-not-sent}} The READMEs describe these fields as scan metadata {{divergence:scan-metadata}}.

checks.do: Whether AIGUARD_POLICY_ID is set and numeric: a non-numeric value is dropped silently and the key's own policy is applied, while a numeric ID the key cannot use fails closed.
Whether on_error is "allow" anywhere the integration is constructed; that turns a missing key, an unreachable API or a verdict-less response into a pass.

The per-scan timeout the integration really uses (10 s for AgentCore and Strands regardless of AIGUARD_TIMEOUT, AIGUARD_TIMEOUT or 30 s for the boto3 hook and the Lambda decorator) before sizing a Lambda or agent time budget.
To find a scan in the AI Guard console, use the scan_transaction_id the API returned, not the app name, session or user, which never reach AI Guard.

bearer-https.statement: The scan request carries the key as a Bearer token; the client refuses an endpoint that is not `https://` (reported as a scan error) and refuses HTTP redirects, so the key is never re-sent to another host.

quotes: """A redirect would re-send the Bearer key to whatever host the 3xx names; refuse."""
**HTTPS is enforced and redirects are refused.** A 3xx would otherwise re-send your API key to whatever host the redirect names.

read-bounds.statement: The scan response is read against one wall-clock deadline rather than a per-read socket timeout, and a body over 10 MB is refused; either outcome is a scan error.

quotes: **Response reads are bounded by a wall-clock deadline and a size cap.**
`urlopen(timeout=)` restarts on every successful read, so a peer that trickles a body could otherwise hold the caller far past its budget.
raise TimeoutError("AI Guard response exceeded the scan deadline")
and a scan response is capped at 10 MB; exceeding either follows the `on_error` posture

payload-fields.statement: Every module's scan body is `content` and `direction`, plus `transactionId` when it has one and `policyId` when a policy ID is configured; a leg's text is flattened into the single `content` string.

quotes: Flatten a leg's content list into (text, direction) for the scan API.

transaction-id.statement: An ID that is not already a UUID (a Lambda request ID, a caller's session string) is hashed into a UUID with uuid5 before it is sent as `transactionId`; the modules' notes say AI Guard rejects a non-UUID `transactionId` with HTTP 500.

quotes: AI Guard rejects a transactionId that is not a standard 36-character UUID
with an HTTP 500, and callers pass request ids and session strings.

policy-id-parsing.statement: Each module takes the policy ID from the `policy_id` argument it is given in code, else `AIGUARD_POLICY_ID`, strips surrounding quotes, and converts it with int(); an empty value or one int() rejects becomes None, the no-policy-ID path.

malformed-id-autoresolves.statement: A non-numeric AIGUARD_POLICY_ID (a policy name, a UUID, a typo with letters) is dropped without a warning and the integration calls resolve-and-execute-policy, so the key's bound policy is applied instead of failing; only a numeric ID the key cannot use reaches execute-policy and fails closed on the verdict-less reply.
malformed-id-autoresolves.conditions: Follows from the parsing and endpoint choice in the four modules; no log line is written on the int() failure (the except branch only returns None). Not exercised against the live API.

verdict-mapping.statement: The verdict's `action` is upper-cased: BLOCK blocks, ALLOW and DETECT allow (DETECT is treated as monitor-only), a response with no action is a scan error that names the in-body `statusCode` and `errorMsg`, and any other action is an 'unknown scan action' error.

timeout-defaults.statement: The AgentCore guard and the Strands provider default `timeout` to 10.0 seconds in their constructors; the boto3 hook and the Lambda decorator default it to `_default_timeout()`, which reads `AIGUARD_TIMEOUT` and falls back to 30.

quotes: scan_timeout = _default_timeout() if timeout is None else timeout

timeout-env-ignored.statement: In the AgentCore guard and the Strands provider `AIGUARD_TIMEOUT` has no effect: each module defines `_default_timeout()` but never calls it, so a scan is bounded by the constructor's 10 seconds unless `timeout=` is passed.
timeout-env-ignored.conditions: Rests on a search of both files at the pin: the only occurrence of _default_timeout in each is its definition.

identity-not-sent.statement: App name, end user, model and agent identifiers never reach AI Guard: the AgentCore guard and the Lambda decorator write them only to their local log line, and the boto3 hook and the Strands provider store them and use them nowhere.

quotes: # Caller identity for the log line only. AI Guard's detection API

identity-not-sent.conditions: The payload construction is quoted; that the boto3 hook and Strands provider never read app_name, app_user, ai_model or agent_meta after the constructor rests on a search of both files at the pin.

session-not-sent.statement: A caller-supplied session ID never becomes the `transactionId`: AgentCore, Lambda and Strands send `transaction_id or session_id`, and the transaction ID is always set first (an explicit ID, the AgentCore or Lambda request ID, or a fresh uuid4), so the session only reaches the log line, if anywhere.
session-not-sent.conditions: Follows from Python's `or` on a value the code always sets; the boto3 hook generates a uuid4 per call and does not read session_id at all.

logging.statement: Each leg writes one JSON line on the `aiguard` logger, allows and other neutral outcomes at INFO and blocks and errors at WARNING. The AgentCore, Lambda and Strands lines carry the integration's own `transaction_id` and, as `scan_transaction_id`, the ID AI Guard assigned, which is the one to search in the console; the boto3 hook writes the API's ID over `transaction_id` when the verdict has one. Without a configured handler Python prints only WARNING and above, so allows are dropped.

quotes: Every leg emits one JSON line on the `aiguard` logger: **allows at INFO, blocks and
errors at WARNING**. Python's last-resort handler only prints WARNING and above, so
`transaction_id` is the id this guard generated for the call; `scan_transaction_id`
is the one the API assigned -- use that to find the record in the AI Guard Console.

# Neutral outcomes read as INFO: an allow, and unscannable content when
        # the posture lets it through. A block or an error is a WARNING.

timeout-default.summary: What per-scan timeout the AWS integrations use by default.

positions.says: The AWS README and each module's docstring say AIGUARD_TIMEOUT sets the per-scan timeout and defaults to 30 seconds.

quotes: | `AIGUARD_TIMEOUT` | no | Seconds per scan call, defaults to `30` |

positions.says: The AgentCore guard's constructor defaults timeout to 10.0 and stores it; its AIGUARD_TIMEOUT reader is never called.
The boto3 hook's README gives a 10-second default, while its code falls back to AIGUARD_TIMEOUT or 30.
The Lambda decorator's README configuration block shows timeout=10.0, while its code defaults to AIGUARD_TIMEOUT or 30 (as its own Limitations section says).

quotes: timeout=10.0,                   # seconds per scan (two scans per invocation)

timeout-default.impact: A time budget sized from the README is wrong for at least one integration: AgentCore and Strands ignore AIGUARD_TIMEOUT and wait 10 s per scan, the boto3 hook and the Lambda decorator wait 30 s unless AIGUARD_TIMEOUT or timeout= is set. The code paths are timeout-defaults and timeout-env-ignored.

scan-metadata.impact: An operator expecting app, user or session attribution in the AI Guard console for these integrations gets none; only the transaction ID correlates a scan with the integration's log line. What the code sends is in payload-fields, identity-not-sent and session-not-sent.
